cookies_description: The one cookie elliotleelewis.com’s host may set, and what the game remembers.
cookies_intro: This site doesn’t set any cookies of its own, and nothing on it tracks you. The only cookie you might get comes from Cloudflare, which hosts the site, and only to keep it secure.
cookies_cloudflare_body: When Cloudflare’s bot protection can’t tell whether a visit comes from a person, it asks your browser to pass a quick check. This cookie remembers that you passed, so you aren’t checked again on every page.
cookies_set_by_value: Cloudflare, only if you’re asked to pass a check
cookies_purpose_value: Security: telling people from bots. It isn’t used to identify or follow you.
cookies_kept_for_value: As long as the check lasts, 30 minutes by default
cookies_cloudflare_more: Read more in Cloudflare’s own list of its cookies
cookies_game_body: The game keeps your best score, the easter eggs you’ve found and the initials you last put on the leaderboard in your browser’s local storage, so they’re still there next time you play. They never leave your device. You can clear them here, or by clearing your browser’s data for this site.
cookies_game_cleared: Cleared. The game will start afresh.
cookies_board_body: If a run makes the game’s leaderboard and you save it, Cloudflare stores your three initials, trees and distance for everyone to see. Nothing else about you is kept. Saving a score first asks Cloudflare Turnstile to check you’re a person, not a bot. It’s only loaded when you save a score.
cookies_analytics_body: I count visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sets no cookies, stores nothing on your device and doesn’t fingerprint you.

intro_bio: I’m a front-end engineer with nearly a decade of building enterprise and consumer web apps, from factory-floor systems at Jabil to Lens creator tools at Snap. I like leading projects and teams, launching products people actually use, and leaving codebases easier to work in than I found them.

trail_snap_event_insights: Led Event Insights end to end across three teams: {#strong}patented{/strong} ({#link}US11894989B2{/link}) and launched at Snap Partner Summit 2022, giving Lens creators new metrics on their lenses.
trail_snap_payouts: Led a four-team effort to build an engagement-based monthly payout program for Lens creators, driving Lens submissions up {#strong}300%{/strong} in its first month.
trail_snap_load_times: Cut My Lenses load times by {#strong}~40%{/strong} and grew end-to-end coverage of our P0 test cases from {#strong}20% to 75%{/strong}, so we could release faster.
trail_snap_digital_goods: Built tooling in My Lenses for creators to manage their digital goods, plus an internal payout system, letting some creators earn thousands of dollars a month.
trail_snap_alerting: Set up real-time error reporting and alerting, bringing mean time to resolve production issues under two hours.
trail_snap_mentoring: Mentored junior engineers, including an apprentice assigned to work on My Lenses.
trail_jabil_architect: Became the de facto front-end architect for {#strong}10+ teams{/strong}, merging a fleet of on-prem front ends into a single regional cloud application.
trail_jabil_redesign: Led a team of 7 engineers redesigning every screen of our {#strong}450k+ line{/strong} flagship application.
trail_jabil_inner_source: Started Jabil’s first inner-source project: an Angular component library for any team in the company.
trail_jabil_jemsmm: Joined a sprint team on JEMSmm (part of the Factory of the Future initiative) as a full-stack developer, building Angular front ends and ASP.NET Core APIs.
trail_jabil_ui_ux: Revived our UI/UX community group and became one of the UI/UX leads for the whole Factory of the Future initiative.
trail_jabil_cio: Recognised by Jabil’s CIO, May Yap, for technical expertise.
trail_jabil_ui_library: Built an Angular UI package library that our team used across every front end in iFactory.
trail_jabil_microsoft: Partnered with a Microsoft team, building an Angular front end for the ASP.NET Core API they’d built.
